move: dot grid sized by brightness of drifting aurora and roaming light
how: A canvas paints a low-res source each frame: three coloured aurora ribbons (mint, periwinkle, pink) whose vertical position and thickness ripple with sine waves that travel across the frame 1 or 2 cycles per D, plus a white radial light that roams on a Lissajous path (cos once, sin twice per D). The output is a 16px grid of dots on near-black, each dot radius rising with source luminance to the 1.3 power and coloured slightly brighter than the source pixel, so bright regions bloom into large dots and dark sky vanishes. All motion is periodic in D.
adapt: Replace drawSource with the product image or brand gradient (same-origin), change the ribbon colours, CELL size and the luminance exponent for contrast. Keep the roaming light for life across a still image.
port: mount(el, shot) creates the output and offscreen canvases; animate(el, shot, D) returns a timeline with one linear progress tween over D whose onUpdate draws the source and the dot grid, replacing fx.register. gsap.min.js is loaded but unused.
caveats: loads gsap but does not use it
per-frame getImageData and about 3600 arcs; fine at this size
